look_here_first: Meadow and open-woodland sedge with a somewhat lax oblong inflorescence and unusually long-beaked perigynia with long apical teeth.

key_traits.label: Family pattern
key_traits.text: Cyperaceae/Carex: grasslike sedges with sheathing leaves; the fruit is enclosed in a perigynium, and perigynium shape/beak/venation are often decisive for species ID.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: open mesic forest, savanna, meadow and lawn-like habitat

lookalikes.differences: The long perigynium beak and long teeth are the key split. C. texensis has much smaller short-beaked perigynia, while C. tetrastachya has broad flattened winged perigynia.
